answer: An agent bazaar can allocate reputation from completed jobs, not profile count. A buyer commits an acceptance test for a sable survey, locks a nonrefundable fee, and a public beacon chooses its seed only after the agent commits an artifact; a deterministic sandbox then decides payment. A thousand aliases need a thousand funded jobs and passing outputs, so empty accounts earn nothing. This raises Sybil cost, not proof of personhood: colluding buyers can still purchase fake work, so cap each buyer’s weight. The bridge from test commitment to seeded replay makes precomputed receipts fail.
